pcs.pc_description: check all piping connections, valves, and hoses for visible leaks or signs of wear and tear, and inspect the nozzle for damage, cracks, or debris that could impede proper fuelling
ensure that the safety latch functions smoothly

identify potential malfunctions by following multiple test procedures like visual inspection, pressure test, flow rate test, temperature monitoring, nozzle and hose functionality, communication and control system test and safety system test
ensure all hub systems are turned on and operational, including hydrogen supply, compressor, cooling system and communication channel
follow the manufacturer's specific instructions for starting the dispenser unit with a key, PIN code, or any other authentication and activate the pump in the dispenser unit
observe pressure gauges and flow indicators to verify proper operation and identify any abnormalities
check the breakaway coupling and Inline breakaway coupling for additional safety
ensure the nozzle is clean and retracted, ready for connection
ensure the check valve is functioning correctly to prevent backflow and potential hazards
identify incompatible vehicles and refuse refuelling
identify whether the vehicle operates on liquid hydrogen or hydrogen fuel cell and use appropriate refuelling technique
guide the vehicle in position, and if equipped, activate the automatic vehicle identification system
ensure the vehicle’s engine and all electrical systems are turned off and parking brakes are engaged
connect the vehicle to a grounding point to prevent static electricity build-up
connect the nozzle securely to the vehicle's fuelling port manually or through automated guidance
initiate a pre-check sequence to test for leaks and confirm proper pressure connection before engaging in fuelling
safely remove hydrogen from vehicles using defueling nozzle, if needed
choose appropriate hydrogen dispensing equipment depending upon the vehicle type; slow- fill for light FCEVs and fast-fill for Heavy-duty FCEVs (buses & trucks)
select the appropriate fuel level or target pressure on the control panel
activate the fuelling handle or trigger on the control panel to initiate refuelling
follow optimal protocols for refuelling, such as SAE J2601, ISO 17266 and PRHYDE Project, depending on factors like vehicle type, ships/vessels hub capabilities, and local regulations
ensure the ship manoeuvres into the designated refuelling zone alongside the bunker barge or onshore hub, deploying mooring lines for stability
choose a compatible fuelling nozzle for ships and vessels
establish communication channels between the ship and hub for coordination and authorisation of the refuelling process
use specialised hoses and connectors designed for high-pressure hydrogen transfer to the ship/vessels
equalise the pressure in the ship's tanks slowly with the refuelling system to avoid pressure surges
commence the controlled flow of hydrogen from the hub to the ship's storage tanks, keeping the flow rate in accordance with the ship's capacity and hub capabilities
monitor dispenser and vehicle tank temperatures during fuelling and adjust flow rate if necessary to prevent overheating
observe real-time data on the control panel, including pressure, flow rates, total dispensed volume, and any system status messages
monitor pressure gauge fluctuations, abnormal valve behaviour, or excessive condensation build-up that could indicate system issues
pay attention to any audible or visual alerts on the control panel that may indicate equipment malfunctions
remove the nozzle from the fuel receptacle and stop the fuelling process once the desired amount of hydrogen is dispensed or the tank reaches full
ensure that the residual pressure is released before disconnecting the nozzle
follow the manufacturer's instructions to properly shut down the dispensing system, including pumps, compressors, and communication channels

pcs.pc_description: regularly inspect gauges and indicators for abnormal readings
calibrate hydrogen dispensing equipment regularly according to SOP and manufacturer specifications
perform routine maintenance tasks on hub equipment, such as compressor functioning, filter changes and lubrication
identify and report potential equipment malfunctions or performance issues to maintenance personnel promptly
maintain accurate records of equipment calibration, maintenance activities, and performance data
stay informed about the latest regulations related to hydrogen production, storage and refuelling
keep away any ignition sources from hydrogen storage areas and maintain a strict no- smoking policy within this zone
ensure hazardous areas and equipment are clearly marked with appropriate signage and warnings

use specialised Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for working in a hydrogen environment, such as flame-resistant suits made from non-static material, goggles and face shields to protect against pressure-driven debris, gloves (neoprene or nitrile), safety boots, respirators and hearing protection for noisy areas
wear appropriate cryogenic protective clothing and gloves when handling liquid hydrogen
report any non-compliance issues promptly to relevant personnel
liaise with regulatory authorities during inspections and audits
adhere to safety protocols when using materials, tools, and equipment
refer to relevant safety standards and guidelines like IEC 61508, NFPA 2, and industry best practices for identifying hydrogen process hazards

use various hydrogen flame detection methods at hydrogen refuelling hubs, such as Ultraviolet (UV) Flame Detectors, Infrared (IR) Flame Detectors, Multi-spectrum Detectors, Video Image Flame Detectors (VIFDs), etc.
use pressure relief valves and automatic shut-off mechanisms to prevent the uncontrolled release of hydrogen
use oil-free equipment compatible with pure oxygen to avoid combustion risks
choose electrical equipment rated for Zone 0 or Zone 1 depending on the potential hydrogen concentration and risk of ignition
utilise intrinsically safe tools and components that eliminate the risk of sparking, such as sealed switches, capacitors, and motors
implement various control measures, such as pressure relief valves, explosion suppression systems, leak detection systems, interlocks and automated safety systems
vent hydrogen to a safe, designated area well away from ignition sources, using a dedicated vent stack designed for high-pressure hydrogen release
dilute oxygen with an inert gas like nitrogen before venting to decrease its concentration and mitigate fire risks
follow first aid instructions appropriately
move yourself or the injured person away from the source of the cryogenic liquid or gas to stop further exposure
rewarm the affected area using lukewarm water (around 38°C or 100°F), in case of cryogenic burns
raise the affected area above the heart level (if possible) to reduce swelling and pain for of cryogenic burns
move the injured person to fresh air and loosen any constricting clothing, if the person is exposed to a toxic gas
perform the Heimlich manoeuvre or chest thrusts as appropriate
start CPR if the person is not breathing and has no pulse
use appropriate fire extinguishers compatible with hydrogen and fire hoses to isolate the fire at the source
wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) when handling or using extinguishers in a hydrogen environment
operate emergency shutdown procedures in case of leaks, pressure spikes, or other safety concerns and activate alarms as necessary
respond promptly and effectively to emergencies and potential hydrogen leaks, including evacuation procedures, communication with emergency services, and implementation of emergency response plans
